# Wax Coat — Vetta Edition

A complete worked example of this system ships alongside this spec as `demo.html`: every rule below applied to one real page, including its mobile layout and a set of deliberately off-style counter-examples. It is the reference for what "on-style" looks like here.

## Atmosphere
A finish plate pulled from a materials index and set on cool paper. The
plate is the picture: mineral plaster with a visible tooth, and one matte
wax coat along its foot. The name of the finish sits in the margin, large
and quiet. Space around the plate is the margin of the index, not an empty
room. Nothing shines, nothing is round, nothing illustrates a place.

Fits a finish schedule, a sample request, a plaster or wax specification,
a material library. It is a poor fit for weather, reservations, diaries,
games, and anything that needs a badge or a mascot.

## Color roles
All colors come from `theme.css` tokens — never hardcode hex in frames.
- `surface` is the index paper, cool and slightly green-gray. `surface-raised`
  is a lighter sheet, used only if a second note must sit on the paper. Do
  not build cards from it.
- `plaster` is the body of the plate. `pit` is the darker mineral speck in
  the tooth. Neither is a panel behind type.
- `surface-foreground` and `primary` are the same ink. The action is ink,
  not a bright fill. `primary-foreground` is paper, for type that sits on
  the wax coat.
- `muted` is the specification label. It stays readable.
- `accent` and `wax` are the coat. `wax` is the band. `accent` colors one
  eyebrow and the focus ring. The coat is not a button and not a page
  background.
- `danger` is a dried red for a refused plate. The word "refused" is required.
- `border` is the hairline around the plate and between specification rows.
  One pixel. It does not frame the page.

## Typography
System stacks only. No webfonts.
- The finish name is a text serif at weight 400, 72–104px, tight line-height,
  slight negative tracking. Never black, never condensed, never all capitals.
- The eyebrow, the specification, and the request are a grotesque, 12–13px,
  uppercase, tracking near 0.18em.
- The sentence under the name is the same serif, 18px, measure under 32
  characters.
- The plate number impressed in the plaster is the serif at 22px, in `pit`,
  low contrast on purpose.
- Type on the wax coat is the grotesque, 12px, `primary-foreground`.
- Scale: name 64/104, sentence 18, eyebrow 12, spec 13, section 36.

## Spacing & layout
- The cover is one plate and one margin, and it fills the first viewport.
  Padding 48. The plate takes the left, about three fifths, and stretches
  to the height of the margin column.
- The name sits at the top of the margin. The specification sits at the
  foot, level with the wax coat. The gap between them is open paper.
- The wax coat is 56px tall, the full width of the plate, along the foot
  only. It is a band, not a scene.
- One column of reading in the margin. A second column would be another plate.
- At 960px the plate stacks above the margin. The plate keeps a fixed height
  near 300px. The name steps to 64px. The request stays a text action with
  a 48px target. Specification rows stay full width.

## Components
- **Plate:** `plaster` fill, mineral tooth from two speck densities in `pit`,
  a 1px `border`, and `shadow-md` so it sits on the paper. Radius 0. No
  picture inside it.
- **Wax coat:** 56px, `wax`, a 1px lighter lip along its top edge. One per
  plate. A second coat is a different plate.
- **Specification row:** label in `muted`, value in ink, separated by 1px
  `border`. No icons, no chips.
- **Request:** tracked uppercase grotesque, 1px `border` underline, not a
  filled shape. Hover moves the underline to `accent`. It does not grow a
  shadow.
- **Refused:** the word in `danger`, same size as a label. It does not
  replace the plate.
- **Focus:** `shadow-focus`. Other shadows belong only to the plate.
- **Radius:** the whole scale is 0.

## Motion
- `duration-still` (160ms). The underline changes color. Nothing travels.
- On a touch screen there is no hover. Press sets the request color to
  `accent`.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, the color change remains.

## Don't
- No gloss, no gradient wash, no beads, no round gel, no color fog.
- No pills, no thick black sticker borders, no hard offset shadows.
- No bronze hairline as the only ornament, and no empty stone field where
  the plate should be. The plate is the mass.
- No washi, no tilted print, no punched ticket, no kraft desk.
- No gold fan, no lacquer night, no emerald jewel.
- No cloth measurements, no book spines, no hazard stripe.
- No second metal. The wax is the only warm dark.
- No bold grotesque headline. The serif names the finish; the grotesque
  specifies it.

# GitHub — Vetta Edition

A complete worked example of this system ships alongside this spec as `demo.html`: every rule below applied to one real page, including its mobile layout and a set of deliberately off-style counter-examples. It is the reference for what "on-style" looks like here.

## Atmosphere
A developer's night desk. Dimmed navy-black panels, quiet borders, green for
"go" and blue for "link". Functional, information-first, zero glamour.

## Color roles
All colors come from `theme.css` tokens — never hardcode hex in frames.
- `surface` (#0d1117) page; `surface-raised` (#161b22) for headers, cards,
  code blocks.
- `primary` green means action/success: the merge/submit button, open state.
- `accent` blue for links, mentions, counters, focus.
- `danger` red for conflicts/deletions/diff minus; text `surface-foreground`,
  secondary `muted`; every box is closed by a 1px `border`.

## Typography
System font stack only:
- Headings small and matter-of-fact: `font-semibold` 16–24px.
- Body 14px; metadata 12px `muted`.
- `font-mono` is half the interface: code, diffs, hashes, branch names, in
  bordered `surface-raised` chips.

## Shape & depth
- Uniform `rounded-md` (6px) on nearly everything.
- Flat by default — borders carry the structure; `shadow-md`/`shadow-lg` only
  for menus and dialogs.

## Components
- Buttons: h-8, `rounded-md`, bordered; primary is filled green, everything
  else is `surface-raised` with border.
- Labels: colorful bordered pills at 12px (use `accent`/`primary`/`danger`
  at ~15% background opacity with matching text).
- Comment/issue boxes: bordered `surface-raised` header + `surface` body.
- Diff rows in `font-mono` 12px: added lines tinted `primary/15`, removed
  `danger/15`.

## Layout
Left-aligned utilitarian columns; container ~1216px, main+sidebar (~296px)
split. Spacing 8/16/24; boxes stack with 16px gaps. Dense but never cramped.

## Don'ts
- No pure black or pure white surfaces; stay in the dimmed palette.
- Green never decorates — only actions/success states.
- No borderless floating cards; if it groups content, it has a border.

# Field Drawer — Vetta Edition

A complete worked example of this system ships alongside this spec as `demo.html`: every rule below applied to one real page, including its mobile layout and a set of deliberately off-style counter-examples. It is the reference for what "on-style" looks like here.

## Atmosphere
A drawer pulled from a field cabinet and left open on the bench. The board
is khaki. Eight finds sit in a darker recess, each one a block of its own
material, each one numbered. The ledger on the right repeats those numbers
with a depth. Nothing depicts a landscape. The tray is the picture.

Fits a collection, a dig log, a materials intake, a conservation bench.
It is a poor fit for weather, travel posters, games, and anything that
needs a mascot or a hazard stripe.

## Color roles
All colors come from `theme.css` tokens — never hardcode hex in frames.
- `surface` is the khaki board. `surface-raised` is the lighter face of a
  pale specimen, not a card behind type.
- `recess` is the tray bed, darker than the board, so the blocks sit down
  into it. It is not a panel for text.
- `chalk`, `bone`, `sand`, `clay`, `shale`, `oxide`, `slate`, and `char`
  are the eight finds. They are the only fills that large. One block, one
  material. Do not gradient them into each other.
- `surface-foreground` and `primary` are the same ink. `primary-foreground`
  is the light face used on `shale`, `oxide`, `slate`, and `char`.
- `muted` is the depth and the bench note. It stays readable on khaki.
- `accent` is oxidized clay. It colors the bench eyebrow and the focus
  ring. It is not a second specimen and not a stripe.
- `danger` is a dried red for a voided find. The word "voided" is required.
- `border` is the hairline between ledger rows and around the recess.
  One pixel. It does not frame the page in black.

## Typography
System stacks only. No webfonts.
- The site name is a text serif at weight 400, 56–72px, tight line-height,
  sentence case. Never black, never condensed, never all capitals.
- Find numbers, the drawer label, and the ledger are a grotesque, 12–13px,
  uppercase, tracking near 0.14em.
- The sentence under the site name is the same serif, 18px, measure under
  36 characters.
- Type on a dark find is the grotesque, 13px, `primary-foreground`.
- Scale: site 40/68, sentence 18, eyebrow 12, ledger 13, section 36.

## Spacing & layout
- The cover is one recess and one ledger, and it fills the first viewport.
  Padding 28. The recess takes about three fifths and stretches to the
  height of the ledger.
- Eight blocks, four across and two down, gap 10. Each block is a face,
  not a thumbnail. Number at the top, material and depth at the foot.
- The site name sits at the top of the ledger column. The eight rows fill
  the middle. The request sits at the foot, level with the last block.
- One column of reading beside the tray. A second column would be another
  drawer.
- At 860px the recess stacks above the ledger and keeps a height near
  420px. The grid becomes two columns and four rows. The site name steps
  to 40px. The request stays a text action with a 48px target.

## Components
- **Recess:** `recess` fill, `shadow-md` pressed into the board, a 1px
  `border`. Radius 0. No picture inside it.
- **Find:** one material token, `shadow-sm` as a lit top edge. Number,
  material, depth. No icon, no rounded pebble, no illustrated bone.
- **Ledger row:** number and material in ink, depth in `muted`, separated
  by 1px `border`. The row count matches the tray.
- **Request:** tracked uppercase grotesque, 1px `border` underline, not a
  filled shape. Hover moves the underline to `accent`. It does not grow a
  shadow.
- **Voided:** the word in `danger`, same size as a label, under the
  request. It does not replace a block.
- **Focus:** `shadow-focus`. The recess is the only mass with depth.
- **Radius:** the whole scale is 0.

## Motion
- `duration-still` (160ms). The underline changes color. Blocks do not lift.
- On a touch screen there is no hover. Press sets the request color to
  `accent`.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, the color change remains.

## Don't
- No sky, no sun, no grass, no dune, no cartoon bone, no explorer costume.
- No hazard stripe, no stencil poster, no yellow on concrete.
- No white linework on a Prussian field. This is a tray, not a plan.
- No ice cores, no plaster tooth, no wax band, no honed-stone emptiness.
- No pills, no thick sticker borders, no hard offset shadows.
- No gradient that melts one find into the next. Each block is a single face.
- No second accent. Oxide is the eyebrow and the focus, not a decoration.

# Geometric Bold — Vetta Edition

A complete worked example of this system ships alongside this spec as `demo.html`: every rule below applied to one real page, including its mobile layout and a set of deliberately off-style counter-examples. It is the reference for what "on-style" looks like here.

## Atmosphere
A Bauhaus poster that happens to be an interface. Flat planes of pure ink on
white, cut by 4px black rules; circles, squares and triangles carry the meaning
before any word does. Nothing recedes, nothing glows, nothing is soft — the page
is loud on purpose and reads as artwork first, UI second.

Fits art exhibitions, design studios, portfolios, and products that want to look
declarative rather than friendly.

## Color roles
All colors come from `theme.css` tokens — never hardcode hex in frames.
- `surface` is white and stays white; `surface-raised` is also white, because
  panels are separated by `border` (4px black), never by fill or elevation.
- `primary` is pure black: body text, every border, and inverted hero blocks
  (black panel + `primary-foreground` text).
- `muted` (earth brown) is the only secondary text color. There are no grays in
  this system — a dimmed gray reads as a mistake here.
- `accent` (blue) is the general emphasis ink: links, selected state, one
  supporting block per screen.
- `danger` (red) is the loudest ink. It doubles as the hero color block, so
  spend it once per screen and let error states own it everywhere else.
- `block-red` / `block-blue` / `block-yellow` / `block-earth` are the four poster
  inks for decorative shapes, each with a matching `-foreground` token.
- Cap any one screen at three inks + black + white. Four is already too many.

## Typography
- Headings: `font-black uppercase tracking-tight`. Weight 900 is the floor, not
  a peak — there is no such thing as a light heading here.
- Hero type is deliberately oversized and allowed to crop or run off the edge:
  roughly 60px → 96px → 160px across sm/md/lg.
- Scale below the hero: H1 36/60, H2 30/36, H3 20/24, body 14/16, small 12/14.
- Body is `font-sans font-medium` — never `font-light` or `font-normal`.
- `font-mono` for numbers, labels, captions and metadata; uppercase with wide
  tracking makes it read as part of the poster grid.
- Button and label text is `uppercase tracking-widest`.

## Spacing & layout
- Asymmetry is the layout rule. Offset the grid, let one column outweigh the
  other, hang shapes off the margin. A centered, evenly balanced page kills the
  style.
- Section rhythm: 48px → 96px → 128px vertical. Container padding 16 → 32 → 48.
- Gaps come in three steps: 8/16, 16/32, 32/48 (small / medium / large).
- Cards pad 24 → 32.
- Blocks butt directly against each other with no gutter — shared 4px rules are
  a feature, and full-bleed color panels should touch the viewport edge.

## Components
- **Borders:** 4px `border` on essentially every container. 8px for a hero
  frame, 2px only for dense table rules.
- **Radius:** `radius-*` are all 0 — hard corners. The single exception is
  `radius-full` for true circles (avatars, dots, badges, round buttons). Nothing
  in between; a 12px rounded card is off-style.
- **Buttons:** solid ink fill (`primary`, `danger`, `accent`) or white with a
  4px black border. `font-bold uppercase tracking-widest`, square corners, no
  shadow. Hover swaps the fill and text colors outright rather than shading them.
- **Cards:** white, 4px black border, flat. Hierarchy is expressed by size and
  by which ink the header block uses, not by elevation.
- **Inputs:** white field, 4px black border, `font-medium`. Focus removes the
  default outline and fills the field with `block-yellow` — the loudest possible
  focus signal, and the reason yellow is reserved.
- **Overlays:** dialogs and popovers sit on white with a 4px border and
  `shadow-lg`, which is a hard 8px black offset with zero blur. That offset is
  the only depth cue this system permits.
- **Decorative shapes:** circles, squares and triangles in the block inks,
  placed to break the grid. They may overlap and crop; they never carry text
  that matters unless the contrast pair is a `block-*` / `-foreground` match.
- **States:** cover default, hover, keyboard focus, active, disabled, loading,
  empty, error and success. Express disabled with a hatched or outlined
  treatment rather than by lowering opacity.

## Motion
- Short and mechanical: `transition-colors` at 200ms. Color swaps, not fades.
- Hover scales up ~5%, active presses down to ~95%. Nothing else moves.
- No parallax, no easing flourishes, no fade-in-on-scroll. If a transition needs
  blur or opacity to look good, it doesn't belong here.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` by dropping the scale steps and keeping the
  color change.

## Accessibility
- Black on white is 21:1; keep long-form reading on that pair.
- The block inks land between roughly 3.8:1 and 5.6:1 with their paired
  foregrounds — fine for large `font-black` display type, not for 12px captions.
  Small text on a colored block should move to black on white.
- `muted` brown on white is about 7.5:1 and is the safe secondary text pair.
- Focus must always be visible; the yellow focus fill is the mechanism, so never
  strip it without replacing it with an equally loud indicator.

## Don't
- No gradients, and no soft transitions between colors.
- No shadows with blur — `shadow-sm` and `shadow-md` are `none` by design.
- No rounded corners other than 0 or a full circle.
- No opacity-based dimming (`opacity-50/60/70`) to create hierarchy.
- No light or regular font weights.
- No gray palette (`gray-100`…`gray-400`) for fills or text.
- No symmetrical, evenly centered layouts.
- No more than three inks plus black and white on one screen.
- No decorative frills — texture, glow, inner shadow, glassmorphism.

# Y3K Chrome — Vetta Edition

A complete worked example of this system ships alongside this spec as `demo.html`: every rule below applied to one real page, including its mobile layout and a set of deliberately off-style counter-examples. It is the reference for what "on-style" looks like here.

## Atmosphere
A void, and one object made of liquid metal. The ground is near-black. Type for
the object name is silver, as if milled. A single iridescent orb is the light
source. Specs are hairline rows. Nothing is a window, nothing is frosted, and
nothing tries to look like glass over a city.

Fits future objects, concept tools, and a single-product viewer. It is a poor
fit for reading, commerce grids, and anything that needs many equal items.

## Color roles
All colors come from `theme.css` tokens — never hardcode hex in frames.
- `surface` is the void. `surface-raised` is a recessed spec plate, one step up.
- `surface-foreground` is cool white for specs. `muted` is for units.
- `primary` is the silver metal. `primary-foreground` is the void, for type on
  a silver control. Display type uses `metal` as a fill, not a flat `primary`.
- `accent` is a cold cyan edge. `iris` is the magenta side of the same orb.
  They appear on the orb and on one highlight, not as a palette of buttons.
- `danger` is a hot fault light. Rare.
- `border` is a dim metal edge on spec rows.

## Typography
- A geometric grotesque. The object name is heavy, tight tracking, large.
- Specs are 13–14px, regular, with mono for the figures only.
- Scale: name 56/80, section 28, body 15, spec 13.
- Do not outline the metal type. The gradient fill is the material.

## Spacing & layout
- The object is centered. Specs sit under it in one column, full measure of the
  plate, not a bento of equal cards.
- Padding 24 → 40. The orb may bleed behind the name but not behind spec text.
- One orb. A second orb is a different product.

## Components
- **Orb:** a circle, `metal` mixed with `accent` and `iris` in a conic fill.
  It is not a button.
- **Name:** `metal` clipped to the glyphs.
- **Spec rows:** label in `muted`, value in `surface-foreground`, 1px `border`
  under each row. No cards.
- **Buttons:** silver fill, void type, `radius-md`, `shadow-sm`. Hover adds
  `shadow-md` (a cyan rim). Active removes the rim.
- **Focus:** `shadow-focus` in `accent`.
- **Radius:** small on controls, full only on the orb. No 32px clay corners.

## Motion
- `duration-glide` (180ms). The rim brightens. The orb does not spin forever.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, the orb stays still and the rim change remains.

## Don't
- No backdrop blur, no translucent panels, no night-city photograph.
- No champagne gold, no paper texture, no hazard stripes.
- No rainbow UI. Iridescence lives on the orb and the name only.
- No soft pastel, no rounded marketing hero with three equal features.
- No blur on the type.

# Apple — Vetta Edition

A complete worked example of this system ships alongside this spec as `demo.html`: every rule below applied to one real page, including its mobile layout and a set of deliberately off-style counter-examples. It is the reference for what "on-style" looks like here.

## Atmosphere
Premium air. Soft neutral gray, white product cards, enormous typography and
enormous silence around it. Everything feels machined: perfect curves, perfect
spacing, one blue.

## Color roles
All colors come from `theme.css` tokens — never hardcode hex in frames.
- `surface` (#f5f5f7) is the stage; `surface-raised` (white) for cards/sheets.
- `surface-foreground` near-black ink; long copy in `muted`.
- `primary` (blue) only on links and the single CTA per view.
- `accent` (green) strictly for success/health; `danger` for destructive.

## Typography
System font stack only — it literally is the brand's stack:
- Display headings huge and heavy: `font-semibold tracking-tight` 32–56px.
- Section titles 21–28px; body 17px with `leading-relaxed`; captions 12px.
- Size contrast does the hierarchy — weights stay between 400 and 600.

## Shape & depth
- Generous radii: cards `rounded-xl`/`rounded-2xl` (18–32px); controls curve
  fully (pill buttons).
- Depth is diffuse and quiet: `shadow-sm` resting, `shadow-md` on hover;
  borders almost invisible (`border` only where surfaces touch).

## Components
- Buttons: pill (`rounded-full`), h-9–11; filled blue primary, and the
  signature quiet secondary — blue text link with a chevron.
- Cards: big white `rounded-2xl` blocks with 24–32px padding, image-led.
- Inputs: `rounded-lg`, hairline border, focus ring `primary/30`.
- Segmented controls over tabs; toggles over checkboxes.

## Layout
Centered, symmetric, spacious. Content max ~980px; sections separated by
64–96px; card grids 2–3 columns with 16–24px gaps. Nothing touches an edge.

## Don'ts
- No dense tables or cramped rows — this language is for showcase surfaces.
- Never more than one accent hue per view; no gradients except product art.
- No sharp corners, no heavy borders, no drop shadows with hard edges.

Vetta Design System

Silence, machined.

Enormous type. One blue. Curves that never break.

Learn more Browse components
32px corners · one accent

01 — Scale

Size does the hierarchy

Display headings run 44–80px, section titles 24–32px, body 17px. Weight barely moves — everything sits between 400 and 600 — because contrast comes from size and space, not from bolding things until they shout.

Curves that never break

Cards take 32px corners, controls curve fully into pills, and nothing in the system has a corner sharper than 8px.

See the radius scale

Depth you can barely see

Shadows are wide, soft and almost transparent. Borders appear only where two surfaces genuinely touch.

See the elevation scale

02 — Controls

Pills, segments, switches

A filled blue pill is the single call to action on a view. Everything else is a blue text link with a chevron — the quiet secondary that carries most of the navigation.

Or watch the film
OverviewSpecsCompare Auto sync Beta features

Segmented controls replace tabs and switches replace checkboxes. Both keep the interface reading as a set of physical objects rather than a form.

surface#f5f5f7 · the stage
raised#ffffff · cards
primary#0071e3 · one CTA
accent#34c759 · success only

03 — Mobile

The same air, at a smaller radius

Nothing about the language changes on a phone. Type steps down, cards go to one column, and the radii ease slightly so a 32px corner does not swallow a 300px card — the proportion between the box and its corner is what has to stay constant.

9:41▮▮ ▮
Vetta⌕ ▤

Vetta Design System

Silence, machined.

One blue. Curves that never break.

Learn moreBuy
Curves that never break

32px corners on desktop, 24px here — the ratio is what stays fixed.

Store
Design
Search
Bag
  • TypeHero 80px → 46px → 30px, section titles 44px → 32px, body stays 17px with the same relaxed leading. Weight never rises above 600 to compensate.
  • RadiusCards ease 32px → 24px and inner art 18px → 12px. A corner has to stay proportional to its box; keeping 32px on a narrow card makes it look inflated.
  • GridTwo- and three-column card grids become one column at 20px gaps. Section spacing 88px → 64px — still the most generous thing on the screen.
  • EdgesNothing touches the edge. Page padding never drops below 20px, even at 320px wide.
  • The quiet secondaryBlue text links with chevrons stay exactly as they are. They are already touch-friendly at 19px and they keep the screen free of button clutter.
  • Segmented controlsStay segmented rather than becoming a dropdown, as long as there are three options or fewer. Four or more moves to a sheet.
  • DepthShadow tokens are unchanged. The diffuse, nearly invisible elevation is a signature, and hardening it for small screens is the most common way this language gets lost.

04 — Off-style, for contrast

What breaks the machining

Hard edges, hard shadow 4px corners · 2px black border · an offset shadow with no blur · weight 800. Every one of those is a deliberate rejection of this system's softness.
Same content, on-style 32px radius, white card, no border, a wide shadow at 4% opacity, weight 600. If you can point at the shadow's edge, it is wrong.

Also out: dense tables, cramped rows, a second accent hue in one view, and gradients anywhere except product artwork.

# Tape Diary — Vetta Edition

A complete worked example of this system ships alongside this spec as `demo.html`: every rule below applied to one real page, including its mobile layout and a set of deliberately off-style counter-examples. It is the reference for what "on-style" looks like here.

## Atmosphere
A Thursday that was assembled on a desk, not aligned on a grid. The ground is
kraft. Three objects overlap a little and tilt a little: a print held by one
strip of washi, a pencil note, and a perforated ticket. The mess has a limit.
One tape color, one ink, one day. Nothing is a sticker with a hard shadow,
and nothing is a print shop's crop marks.

Fits a personal week, a small reservation, a note to oneself, a program that
should feel handled. It is a poor fit for dashboards, banking, dense tools,
and anything that must look frictionless.

## Color roles
All colors come from `theme.css` tokens — never hardcode hex in frames.
- `surface` is the kraft desk. `kraft-deep` is a darker fiber used only as a
  corner shade, not as a panel.
- `surface-raised` is the note paper and the print's border. It is warm white,
  never pure white.
- `surface-foreground` and `primary` are the same walnut ink. `primary` is the
  stamp and the ticket's type. `primary-foreground` is paper, for the rare
  solid ink button.
- `muted` is the caption under a print and the small date above the day.
- `accent` is the washi. It is also the notebook rule on the left of the note.
  It is not a button fill.
- `ticket` is the stub's stock, a pale yellow distinct from the note.
- `print` is the flat field inside the print's border. `print-ink` draws the
  object in that field. The field is not a photograph.
- `danger` is for a missed line. The word "missed" is required. It is not the
  stamp and not the tape.
- `border` is walnut ink at 1px, for the stamp's double rule. It does not
  frame the whole page.

## Typography
System stacks only. No webfonts. There is no script face.
- The day is a text serif, weight 400, 64–84px, tight line-height. It is the
  diary's date, not a campaign headline.
- The note is the same serif in italic, 22–26px, the pencil voice. One note
  per page, two short sentences at most: one at the top of the sheet, one
  at the foot.
- The stamp, the ticket, and the caption are a monospace, 12px, uppercase,
  tracking near 0.12em.
- The small date above the day is the serif, 14px, `muted`.
- Scale: day 48/84, note 22/26, stamp 12, caption 12, section 32.

## Spacing & layout
- The cover is one spread and it fills the first viewport. Padding 40px 5.5vw
  36px. The day and the stamp occupy the top band. Everything under them is
  the cluster, stretched to the bottom margin.
- The print is the tall object in the left column. Its drawn field grows with
  the viewport and stays at least 300px, so the lower half of the spread is
  paper and print, not bare kraft.
- The note is a sheet, not a label. It overlaps the print by about 84px,
  stretches the height of the print, and tilts about +2 degrees. One
  sentence sits at the top of the sheet and a second, shorter sentence sits
  at the foot, so the paper between them is part of the note.
- The ticket is the bottom band, up to 860px wide, aligned to the right,
  tilted about −1 degree. It tucks just under the print. Tilts stay under
  6 degrees.
- The stamp sits in the top band at the right, rotated about −8 degrees. It
  is not pinned over the print.
- One tape, across the upper third of the print, extending past both sides.
- At 720px the spread stops stretching with the viewport and becomes one
  column. The note drops first, then the ticket. Tilts fall to about 1 degree
  so nothing clips. The tape stays. Objects take the full content width. The
  day steps down to 48px. The stamp moves under the day, still rotated, before
  the print. The ticket stays at least 48px tall.

## Components
- **Print:** a warm-white border, 12px at the sides and top, 36px at the
  bottom where the caption sits. Inside is a flat `print` field and a drawn
  object in `print-ink`. No external image. Radius 0.
- **Tape:** one strip, about 26px tall, `accent` in two close opacities so it
  looks like washi and not a flat bar. It crosses the print. It is not a
  sticker and has no black outline.
- **Note:** `surface-raised`, an inset 3px `accent` rule on the left, italic
  serif. Soft paper shadow `shadow-md`. No border.
- **Stamp:** double 2px `border`, monospace, uppercase, rotated. It marks the
  date. It is not a status pill.
- **Ticket:** `ticket` stock, holes punched along the left edge, monospace
  facts. The whole stub is the target, at least 48px tall. Radius 0.
- **Focus:** `shadow-focus`, an ink ring. Other shadows are only the soft
  paper lift.

## Motion
- `duration-still` (160ms). Hover may ease a tilt back by 1 degree. Nothing
  bounces, nothing fades up.
- On a touch screen there is no hover. The resting tilt is the look. Press
  darkens the ticket stock slightly.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, tilts stay at rest.

## Don't
- No lime sticker, no thick black outline, no hard offset shadow, no polka dot.
- No crop marks, no halftone, no misregistered second plate, no fluorescent ink.
- No vast empty margin with a single seal. This page is occupied.
- No photographed face, no scraped texture, no external paper scan.
- No pill button, no blurple fill, no rounded app card as the note.
- One tape. A second color of washi means a different day.

# Discord — Vetta Edition

A complete worked example of this system ships alongside this spec as `demo.html`: every rule below applied to one real page, including its mobile layout and a set of deliberately off-style counter-examples. It is the reference for what "on-style" looks like here.

## Atmosphere
A cozy dark clubhouse. Soft charcoal layers (never pure black), blurple
energy, rounded friendly shapes. Gaming DNA: playful, badge-covered, alive.

## Color roles
All colors come from `theme.css` tokens — never hardcode hex in frames.
- Three-layer depth: darkest rail (`surface-raised` darkened — use `black/20`
  overlays), `surface-raised` sidebar, `surface` content.
- `primary` blurple for CTAs, active items, mentions, brand moments.
- `accent` green strictly for online/voice-connected states.
- `danger` for pings and destructive; text `surface-foreground`, secondary
  `muted`.

## Typography
System font stack only:
- Headings `font-bold` 16–20px; channel names 15px `font-medium`.
- Messages 15px `leading-relaxed`; usernames `font-medium` and may take
  role colors (`primary`/`accent`).
- Tiny labels 11–12px `font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide text-muted`
  (category headers).

## Shape & depth
- Everything softly rounded: `rounded-lg` (8px) panels, `rounded-full`
  avatars, pill badges.
- Layer color does the depth; `shadow-lg` only for modals/popouts.

## Components
- Buttons: h-9–11 `rounded-lg`, filled blurple primary; secondary is a
  lighter charcoal fill (no borders).
- Message rows: hover `black/10` wash, floating reaction toolbar.
- Channel list: 32px rows in `muted`, active = white text on `white/10` pill.
- Badges: tiny `rounded-full` counters in `danger` with white 11px bold text;
  status dots (accent green / muted gray) on avatar corners.

## Layout
Rail (72px, circular server icons) + sidebar (240px) + chat + members (240px).
Compact rows, 8/12/16 spacing. The chat column is the hero.

## Don'ts
- Never pure black backgrounds or 1px gray hairline aesthetics — layers, not
  borders.
- Blurple never used for body text; green never decorative.
- No sharp corners anywhere; no thin/light font weights.

# Claymorphism — Vetta Edition

A complete worked example of this system ships alongside this spec as `demo.html`: every rule below applied to one real page, including its mobile layout and a set of deliberately off-style counter-examples. It is the reference for what "on-style" looks like here.

## Atmosphere
Every surface looks moulded out of soft modelling clay: fat rounded corners, a
candy pastel fill, a white sheen along the top edge, and a hard offset drop
beneath that reads as extruded thickness rather than a cast shadow. The page
sits on warm cream with lumps of pastel clay drifting behind the content.
Nothing is sharp, nothing is gray, nothing is flat — and when pressed, pieces
squash and spring back.

Fits kids' products, learning apps, wellness and habit trackers, playful
onboarding, and consumer products that want to feel handmade and harmless. It is
a poor fit for dense dashboards, financial data, or anything that needs to look
authoritative.

## Color roles
All colors come from `theme.css` tokens — never hardcode hex in frames.
- `surface` is warm cream. Backgrounds stay warm: cream, pale amber, very light
  pastel. A white, gray, or dark page kills the style outright.
- `surface-raised` is white, usually set at partial opacity over the cream so
  the page warmth still shows through.
- `primary` is clay pink, the default action color.
- `primary-foreground` is a dark neutral ink. Every tint in this palette is
  light, so white text on clay lands near 2:1 — ink is always dark here.
- `muted` is a *warm* gray for secondary text. Cool, desaturated neutrals read
  as dirt against these pastels.
- `accent` is lavender: secondary actions, selected state, informational tags.
- `danger` is a soft rose, not an alarm red. It signals through its dark ink and
  its label, never through saturation.
- `clay-pink` / `clay-mint` / `clay-lavender` / `clay-yellow` / `clay-cream` are
  the five candy tints, each with a paired `-foreground` ink tuned to its hue —
  plum on pink, deep green on mint, indigo on lavender, amber-brown on yellow
  and cream. Pair them only as matched sets.
- `gradient-page` (cream → pink → lavender) and `gradient-rainbow` (all five
  tints) are for hero surfaces; spend the rainbow once per screen at most.
- `border` is a barely-there warm line. Depth is the shadow pair's job — a
  visible border competes with the highlight and flattens the piece.
- Two or three tints per screen. All five at once reads as a color test.

## Typography
- A geometric sans with open, rounded letterforms throughout, and it must carry
  a real 900 cut. There is no monospace and no condensed face in this system,
  not even for code labels or numerals.
- Display and headings are `font-black` (900); subheads `font-bold`; body
  `font-medium`. A light or regular weight looks brittle against fat shapes.
- Heading ink is the dark neutral, body one step lighter, captions `muted`.
  Colored headings appear only as a gradient-filled accent word in a hero.
- Scale: hero 48/72, H1 36/48, H2 30/36, H3 20/24, body 16, small 14, caption 12.
- Line height is generous — 1.6 for body — so text feels as soft as the
  containers holding it. Measure stays at 65–75 characters.
- No uppercase headlines and no tight negative tracking; letterforms stay wide
  and open.

## Spacing & layout
- Padding is deliberately generous: clay pieces need room or their offset drops
  collide and depth turns into mud. Card padding 24 → 32.
- Section rhythm 64 → 96 vertical; container padding 24 → 32.
- Gaps come in three steps: 16, 24, 32. Never below 16 — adjacent drops must not
  overlap, and the drop needs clearance on the right and bottom.
- Layouts are loose and centered; content sits in a container with wide margins,
  and nothing runs edge-to-edge.
- Background blobs are lumps, not circles: asymmetric radii (`blob-radius`),
  low-saturation tints, scattered behind content and never behind small text.
- Touch targets stay at 44px minimum, which the fat radii already encourage.

## Components
- **Radius:** the scale starts at 16px; `radius-lg` (24px) is the default clay
  corner, `radius-2xl` (32px) for large cards, `radius-full` for buttons, pills,
  avatars and icon holders. There is no small-radius option — a 4px corner is
  off-style, and 0 is forbidden.
- **Shadows:** each piece uses a pair — a zero-blur offset drop plus an inset
  white top highlight. `shadow-sm` for small pieces, `shadow-md` for buttons and
  controls, `shadow-lg` for cards and hero pieces. `shadow-bloom` is the only
  blurred option, a colored halo reserved for a floating hero element.
- **Buttons:** pastel fill (flat tint or `gradient-primary`), `radius-full`,
  bold dark ink, `shadow-md`. Hover swaps to `shadow-hover` and scales to 1.04;
  active drops to `shadow-active` and scales to 0.97 — the drop shrinking under
  the press is what sells the squash. Secondary buttons are the same shape in
  `clay-mint` or `clay-lavender`; a quiet button is `clay-cream` with
  `shadow-sm`. There is no bare text link button.
- **Cards:** white at partial opacity or a single clay tint, 24–32px radius,
  `shadow-lg`, no border. A thin white bar inset near the top edge reinforces
  the moulded sheen.
- **Inputs:** cream field, `radius-xl`, and a highlight-only inner shine so the
  field reads as pressed *into* the page while everything else sits on top of
  it. Focus adds `shadow-focus-ring` and never removes the outline without
  replacing it.
- **Overlays:** dialogs are clay cards on a warm blurred scrim; they keep
  `shadow-lg` and their radius rather than growing a border.
- **Badges, tags, tabs:** `radius-full` pills in a clay tint with `shadow-sm`;
  a tab group is one pill-shaped clay track with the active tab raised inside it.
- **Toggles, sliders, progress:** the track is a recessed clay groove, the thumb
  or fill a raised piece — the same in/out language as inputs.
- **States:** cover default, hover, keyboard focus, active, disabled, loading,
  empty, error and success. Disabled loses its offset drop and keeps a faint
  highlight, so it reads as pressed flat rather than merely faded.

## Motion
- Everything springs: `duration-base` (200ms) with `ease-spring`, whose
  overshoot past 1 is what makes movement read as elastic rather than mechanical.
- Hover scales to ~1.04 and pushes the drop out; active scales to ~0.97 and
  pulls it in. Squash on press, stretch on release — that deformation is the
  signature of the style.
- Entrances scale up from ~0.95 with the same spring. No fades from zero
  opacity, no cross-screen slides, no parallax.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` drop the scale steps and keep the shadow and
  color change, so state stays legible.

## Accessibility
- Every tint is light, so contrast lives entirely in the `-foreground` inks.
  Pair `clay-mint` with `clay-mint-foreground`, never with white.
- Dark neutral ink on cream is roughly 14:1 and is the reading pair for long
  text; `muted` on cream clears 4.5:1 for secondary text only.
- Never set small text on `gradient-rainbow` or across a gradient seam — move it
  onto a solid tint or `surface-raised`.
- Depth is decorative, so state must never be carried by shadow alone; pair it
  with a color, icon, or text change.
- The focus ring is the keyboard affordance; a component that suppresses it owes
  an equally visible substitute.

## Don't
- No sharp or small corners: nothing below 16px, and never 0.
- No `shadow: none` on an interactive piece — a flat clay button is not clay.
- No dark, moody, or high-contrast backgrounds, and no dark-mode inversion of
  this palette. The material only works in light and warm.
- No harsh drop shadows: the offset drop stays under ~0.2 alpha, and blurred
  shadows are limited to the colored bloom.
- No cool grays or desaturated neutrals anywhere, as fill or as text.
- No monospace or condensed typefaces, and no light or regular weights.
- No neon, electric, or fully saturated colors mixed into the pastels.
- No dense layouts where offset drops overlap, and no zero-gap grids.
- No pure black or white text on a clay tint.
- No linear or abrupt easing — motion without spring reads as broken here.

# Firn — Vetta Edition

A complete worked example of this system ships alongside this spec as `demo.html`: every rule below applied to one real page, including its mobile layout and a set of deliberately off-style counter-examples. It is the reference for what "on-style" looks like here.

## Atmosphere
A still-water house at service, the allocation already on the counter. The
ground is pale ice paper, cool and gray, not white and not blue sky. Three
cores stand in a row: pale ice, wet stone, dark slate. They are flat mineral
steps, cut vertical, full height. Type on the paper is deep marine ink. One
steel line, short, sits under the sentence. Nothing fizzes, nothing frosts,
nothing draws a mountain.

Fits a water house, a cold cellar, a mineral ledger, a tasting allocation.
It is a poor fit for weather, soft drinks, spas, and glass dashboards.

## Color roles
All colors come from `theme.css` tokens — never hardcode hex in frames.
- `surface` is the ice paper, on the ledger side. `surface-raised` is a
  lighter chip, used only for a note. Do not build cards from it.
- `band-pale`, `band-mid`, and `band-deep` are the three cores. They are flat
  fills. They are not a gradient and not a horizon. `band-deep-foreground`
  is the type on the slate core. `band-deep-muted` is its secondary line.
- `surface-foreground` and `primary` are the marine ink. The action is ink,
  not a bright fill. `primary-foreground` is the light paper, for type on
  the slate core or on a solid ink control.
- `muted` is the ledger label and the core's secondary line. It stays cool
  and dark enough to read on `band-pale` and on `band-mid`.
- `accent` is steel. It colors one short rule and the words "On service".
  It is not a button, not a band, and not a frost.
- `danger` is a dried red for a lot sent back. The word "Returned" is required.
- `border` is the hairline between ledger rows. One pixel. Core edges meet
  flush; they do not wear a card stroke.

## Typography
System stacks only. No webfonts.
- The source name is a grotesque at weight 500, 96–132px, tight line-height,
  slight negative tracking. One word, or two short lines. Not a serif monument
  and not a black poster.
- The sentence under it is the same grotesque, 18px, weight 400, measure
  under 34 characters.
- Ledger labels are 12px, uppercase, tracked, `muted`. Values are 16–18px
  in the ink.
- Core names are 13px, uppercase, tracked. The temperature is the grotesque
  at 64–80px, weight 400, tabular figures.
- "On service" is 12px, uppercase, tracked, `accent`.
- Scale: name 112, sentence 18, figure 72, ledger 16, label 12.

## Spacing & layout
- The first viewport is the counter. The cores occupy the left, about two
  fifths, and run from the top edge to the bottom edge with no outer margin.
  Three equal vertical columns, flush.
- Each core carries its depth log from just under the name to just above the temperature. The stations are equal rows. They are the body of the sample, not a caption floating in a blank panel.
- The ledger occupies the right, padded 48 → 64. The name sits at the top.
  The steel line sits under the sentence. The rows fill the middle. The
  action and the returned line sit on the bottom edge.
- Ledger rows are equal cells. They tile the open height. A row is a 1px
  rule, a label, and a value.
- One source is on service. The others stay in the rack. A second accent
  rule is off-style.
- At 800px the cores become a row of three vertical slabs, about 240px tall,
  still divided on the vertical. They do not become horizontal stripes. The
  name steps to 64px. Ledger rows stay full width and at least 48px tall.

## Components
- **Core:** a full-height flat fill. Name and place at the top. A depth log
  of ruled stations tiles the body: elevation at the left, a one-word bed
  at the right, in the core's own type color. Temperature sits at the foot,
  with a short rule above the figure. No highlight, no inner shadow, no bubble.
- **On service:** the words, in `accent`, on the pale core only.
- **Steel line:** 64–80px wide, 1px, `accent`. One per screen, under the
  sentence.
- **Ledger row:** label left, value right, 1px `border`. No icons, no chips,
  no meters.
- **Reserve:** tracked uppercase grotesque, 1px `border` underline, target
  at least 44px. Hover moves the underline to `accent`. It does not fill.
- **Returned:** the word in `danger`, same size as a label, under the action.
- **Focus:** `shadow-focus`. Other shadows are `none`.
- **Radius:** the whole scale is 0.

## Motion
- `duration-still` (150ms). The underline changes color. Bands do not melt,
  numbers do not count up.
- On a touch screen there is no hover. Press sets the reserve line to `accent`.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, the color change remains.

## Don't
- No sky, no sun, no grass, no cloud, no weather glyph, no temperature-as-forecast.
- No bubbles, no fizz, no condensation, no rounded glass, no airbrushed frost.
- No blur, no translucent panel, no night scene behind the type.
- No blueprint grid, no white linework on a Prussian field.
- No plaster tooth, no wax band, no warm mineral swatch.
- No bronze hairline on ivory stone, and no serif monument for the source.
- No horizontal stripes that read as a landscape. The cores stand upright.
- No second steel line. The accent is the short rule and the words "On service".

# Anthropic — Vetta Edition

A complete worked example of this system ships alongside this spec as `demo.html`: every rule below applied to one real page, including its mobile layout and a set of deliberately off-style counter-examples. It is the reference for what "on-style" looks like here.

## Atmosphere
A well-bound book. Warm cream paper, dark ink, one clay accent — humanist,
literary, unhurried. Technology presented with the calm of print.

## Color roles
All colors come from `theme.css` tokens — never hardcode hex in frames.
- `surface` (book-cloth cream #f0eee6) is the page; `surface-raised` (white)
  for cards and figures.
- `primary` is INK (#191919): primary buttons are dark ink pills with white
  text.
- `accent` (clay #cc785c) for links, highlights, small illustrations, active
  states — the single warm voice.
- Body text ink; secondary `muted` (warm gray); `border` warm hairlines.

## Typography
System font stack; lean on the serif stack for voice:
- Display/section headings in `font-serif` `font-medium` 28–44px — the
  literary signature.
- Body 15–16px sans with `leading-relaxed`; UI labels 13–14px sans.
- Quotes/figure captions may italicize serif; `font-mono` for code on white
  cards.

## Shape & depth
- Generous soft radii: cards `rounded-xl`/`rounded-2xl` (16–28px), buttons
  `rounded-full` pills.
- Nearly flat: warm borders + white cards on cream; `shadow-md` only for
  overlays. Print doesn't cast shadows.

## Components
- Buttons: pill h-10; primary ink-filled; secondary bordered cream; links in
  clay with underline on hover.
- Cards: white `rounded-2xl` with 24–32px padding, small clay eyebrow label,
  serif title, sans body.
- Callouts: cream-on-cream with a clay left border and serif lead-in.
- Diagrams favor thin ink lines with clay highlights, hand-drawn warmth.

## Layout
Reading column ~720px centered, airy 56–80px section spacing; card grids 2–3
columns with 24px gaps. Margins are generous — the page must feel unhurried.

## Don'ts
- No cool grays or blue-tinted neutrals — every neutral is warm.
- Clay never fills buttons or large areas; it is an accent voice, not a brand
  shout.
- No dark mode, no glossy shadows, no tight dense grids.

Design notes — no. 04

A system set like a well-bound book

Warm cream paper, dark ink, and a single clay voice. The serif carries every heading; the sans carries every sentence you actually have to read at length. Nothing is cool-toned, nothing is glossy, and the page is allowed to be unhurried.

01 — Voice

Two typefaces, one job each

Serif for display, sans for body, mono only where a machine wrote the value. Headings sit at weight 500 — a heavy serif reads as a newspaper, not a book.

Clay is an accent voice, not a brand shout. It underlines, it labels, it draws a line in a figure — it never fills a button. Working rule, page 12
On warmth

Every neutral in this system leans warm. A blue-gray border or a cool #f5f5f5 fill will fight the cream page immediately, even at 1px.

02 — Cards

White paper laid on cream

Surface

28px corners

Cards are generous rectangles of white with warm hairline borders. Depth is the paper contrast, not a shadow.

Rhythm

720px column

The reading measure never widens. Grids sit outside it; prose never does.

Accent

One clay line

An eyebrow label, a quote rule, a link underline. Three appearances per screen is already a lot.

03 — Figures

Thin ink lines, one clay highlight

Diagrams are drawn, not rendered: hairline strokes, open shapes, a single warm emphasis. No gradients, no 3D, no drop shadows on a diagram element.

One value, changed once, arriving everywhere.

04 — Controls

Ink pills

surface#f0eee6 · book cloth
primary#191919 · ink pills
accent#cc785c · clay voice
raised#ffffff · paper

Buttons are full pills at 46px. The clay swatch above is the largest area of accent the system ever shows — and it is a swatch, not a surface.

05 — Mobile

A pocket edition, not a different book

The phone build keeps the serif display, the drop cap and the cream page. What changes is the measure and the margins — the same choices a printer makes going from folio to pocket.

Design notes — no. 04

A system set like a well-bound book

Warm cream paper, dark ink, a single clay voice. The serif carries every heading; the sans carries the sentences.

Accent

  • The measure720px becomes the viewport at 22px gutters. Body text holds 16px/1.75 — a book does not shrink its text to fit a smaller page, it shortens the line.
  • Display type56px → 38px → 25px in the phone frame. Serif headings keep weight 500 at every size; they never bold up to compensate for a small screen.
  • The drop capSurvives, at 40px instead of 62px. It is the one ornament worth keeping on a phone, and it stays clay.
  • CardsThree columns become one stack with 14px gaps. Padding drops 28px → 16px and the radius eases 28px → 20px, so the corner stays proportional to the box.
  • PillsButtons keep the full radius and go full width for the primary action. Height 46px → 42px, still comfortably above the touch minimum.
  • NavigationThe masthead links collapse to a single menu glyph. No bottom tab bar exists — this is a document, and documents scroll.
  • FiguresThin-line diagrams reflow to a vertical stack with the clay arrow rotated. Stroke weight stays 1.25px; hairlines are the drawing style, not a desktop detail.

06 — Off-style, for contrast

What breaks the binding

Cool dark panel Blue-gray neutrals · 6px corner · sans everywhere · glossy shadow · dark mode. Each one on its own is enough to make this stop looking like print.
Same content, on-style Cream page, white card, 28px corner, warm hairline, serif heading at weight 500, no shadow. If it feels unhurried, it is right.

Also out: clay-filled buttons or banners, tight dense grids, cool grays of any kind, and a dark theme — this system has one temperature.

# Travertine — Vetta Edition

A complete worked example of this system ships alongside this spec as `demo.html`: every rule below applied to one real page, including its mobile layout and a set of deliberately off-style counter-examples. It is the reference for what "on-style" looks like here.

## Atmosphere
A room of honed stone, and one object in it. The ground is warm ivory, not
white and not beige-yellow. Type is charcoal. A single bronze hairline is the
only ornament, and it is short. Space is the luxury. Nothing shines, nothing
is striped, nothing asks to be tapped twice.

Fits a gallery viewing, a scent, a vessel, a hotel suite, a maison object.
It is a poor fit for tools, games, weather, and anything that needs a badge.

## Color roles
All colors come from `theme.css` tokens — never hardcode hex in frames.
- `surface` is the stone. `surface-raised` is a lighter slab, used rarely, for
  a sheet of paper on the stone. Do not stack slabs.
- `surface-foreground` and `primary` are the same charcoal. The action is
  charcoal, not a bright fill. `primary-foreground` is the lighter stone, for
  the rare solid button.
- `muted` is for the aside and the dimension. It is still dark enough to read.
- `accent` is bronze. It colors one short rule and one eyebrow. It is not a
  button and not a background.
- `danger` is a dried red for a cancellation. The word is required.
- `border` is the long hairline. One pixel. It separates a list. It does not
  frame a card.

## Typography
- The object name is a text serif at weight 400. Large, 72–112px, tight
  line-height, slight negative tracking. Never black, never condensed.
- Eyebrows and the action are a grotesque, 12px, uppercase, tracking near
  0.2em. They are small so the serif can be large.
- The sentence under the name is the same serif, 18px, measure under 36
  characters. A wide paragraph becomes a website.
- Scale: name 72/112, sentence 18, eyebrow 12, list 16.

## Spacing & layout
- The cover is mostly stone. Padding 64 → 96 on the left. The name sits in
  the upper left, not the center.
- A dimension column may sit at the lower right, far from the name. The gap
  between them is the composition.
- Vertical rhythm inside a group is 28–40. Between groups, 64–96.
- One column of reading. A second column is a caption, not a dashboard.

## Components
- **The bronze rule:** 64–80px wide, 1px, `accent`. One per screen, under the
  name. A full-width bronze bar is off-style.
- **The action:** a tracked uppercase grotesque with a 1px `border` underline,
  not a filled pill. Hover does not grow a shadow. It shortens nothing; the
  underline may shift to `accent`.
- **Lists:** rows separated by 1px `border`, generous vertical padding, label
  left, value right. No cards, no icons.
- **Focus:** `shadow-focus`, a bronze ring. Shadows otherwise are `none`.
- **Radius:** the whole scale is 0.

## Motion
- `duration-still` (160ms). Color of an underline. Nothing travels, nothing
  fades up.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, the same color change remains.

## Don't
- No gloss, no gradient sky, no water beads, no color fogs.
- No pills, no drop shadows, no rounded cards, no photography stand-in boxes.
- No seal, no hazard stripe, no sun disc, no leaf green, no coral.
- No second metal. Bronze once.
- No bold grotesque headline. The serif is the name; the grotesque is the whisper.

# Netflix — Vetta Edition

A complete worked example of this system ships alongside this spec as `demo.html`: every rule below applied to one real page, including its mobile layout and a set of deliberately off-style counter-examples. It is the reference for what "on-style" looks like here.

## Atmosphere
A dark cinema where the interface disappears and posters glow. Black stage,
one red signature, sharp edges, big imagery. Everything says "press play".

## Color roles
All colors come from `theme.css` tokens — never hardcode hex in frames.
- `surface` (#141414) everywhere; `surface-raised` for hover cards and rows.
- `primary` red for THE action (play/subscribe) and the logo moment — nothing
  else is red except `danger` states.
- `accent` green only for match percentages and "new" tags.
- Text white; secondary `muted`; `border` almost never — darkness separates.

## Typography
System font stack only. Cinematic scale:
- Hero titles `font-black tracking-tight` 40–64px, often on imagery.
- Shelf titles 18–20px `font-bold`; card meta 12–13px `muted`.
- Buttons 14–16px `font-semibold`.

## Shape & depth
- Sharp-ish: `rounded-md` (4px) on cards/buttons; nothing bubbly.
- Depth via image glow and `shadow-lg` on the hover-expanded card; gradients
  (black→transparent) anchor text onto artwork.

## Components
- Buttons: `rounded-md` h-10–12; primary solid red; secondary `white/20`
  translucent fill with white text (over imagery).
- Poster cards: 16:9 image, no chrome at rest; on hover scale up with
  `shadow-lg` and reveal a metadata strip on `surface-raised`.
- Hero: full-bleed artwork, left-aligned title block over a horizontal
  gradient, two buttons.
- Badges: tiny red "N", green match % `font-bold`, `muted` maturity chips
  with 1px border.

## Layout
Horizontal shelves over a full-width canvas; rows of 4–6 posters with 8–12px
gaps (tight — imagery forms a wall). Page gutters 40–56px. Vertical rhythm by
shelf (32–40px between).

## Don'ts
- No white backgrounds, no cards with visible borders, no rounded-xl.
- Red never fills panels or decorates text; it is the action color.
- Never crowd artwork with UI chrome — text sits on gradients, not boxes.

01 — Artwork first

The interface disappears

A poster at rest has no border, no label, no radius beyond 4px and no shadow. All of that arrives on hover: the card scales to 1.08, takes shadow-lg, and reveals a metadata strip. Text over artwork always sits on a gradient — never in a box.

primary#e50914 · the action
accent#46d369 · match % only
surface#141414 · the stage
raised#1f1f1f · hover strip

Red belongs to the wordmark, the Top 10 flag and the play button. It never fills a panel, tints a background or colors a paragraph.

02 — Controls

Solid, translucent, done

Secondary buttons are a translucent gray-white fill, because they usually sit on top of artwork and cannot rely on a fixed background. Radius stays at 4px — nothing in this system is bubbly.

03 — Mobile

Landscape shelves become portrait walls

The one real change on a phone is aspect ratio: 16:9 stills give way to 2:3 portrait art, because a phone screen is tall and six thumbnails per row would be unreadable. Everything else — gradients, sharp corners, one red button — is unchanged.

  • Aspect ratio16:9 → 2:3. Three portrait posters per row instead of six landscape ones, still at 6–8px gaps so the artwork keeps forming a wall.
  • HeroThe horizontal scrim becomes a vertical one and the text block centers. Title 68px → 24px; the synopsis is dropped entirely in favour of a genre line.
  • Hover statesThere are none. The scale-and-reveal card becomes a tap that opens the title page, so no metadata is stranded behind an interaction the device cannot perform.
  • ButtonsPlay and My List pair up full width at 32–44px. Play stays white-on-dark; the translucent gray secondary still works over any artwork.
  • ChromeThe top nav collapses to the wordmark and profile over a gradient, never a solid bar. The four destinations move to a bottom tab bar on near-black.
  • Gutters48px → 14px. Artwork is allowed to run closer to the edge on a phone; that is what makes it feel full-bleed.
  • BadgesMatch percentage, maturity chip and the red Top 10 flag all keep their exact desktop treatment — they are small enough to survive untouched.

04 — Off-style, for contrast

What breaks the cinema

Bordered rounded card 18px radius · visible 1px border · a chrome box wrapped around content. Borders and big radii both announce the interface, which is exactly what this system refuses to do.
Same content, on-style
4px radius, no border, artwork to the edges, text sitting on a gradient. Darkness does the separating.

Also out: white backgrounds, red as a panel fill or text color, and any UI chrome crowded on top of artwork without a gradient underneath it.

# Riso Press — Vetta Edition

A complete worked example of this system ships alongside this spec as `demo.html`: every rule below applied to one real page, including its mobile layout and a set of deliberately off-style counter-examples. It is the reference for what "on-style" looks like here.

## Atmosphere
A neighborhood print shop's job desk, not a poster hung on a wall. The page is
uncoated paper with a fine tooth. Work is separated by crop marks, a 1px soy
rule, and a second ink plate that sits a few pixels out of register. Color
arrives as flat spot ink — blue, fluorescent pink, yellow — and where two
plates cross they darken instead of blending through a gradient. Halftone dots
live inside the ink. Nothing is glossy, nothing is soft, nothing is a marketing
hero.

Fits independent presses, editioned goods, cultural programs, music, food, and
any product that should feel printed by a person. It is a poor fit for banking,
dense analytics, long-form reading, and anything that needs to look frictionless
or clinical.

## Color roles
All colors come from `theme.css` tokens — never hardcode hex in frames.
- `surface` is the desk: warm uncoated stock, darker than the sheet. It is never
  pure white and never a cool gray.
- `surface-raised` is the sheet lying on the desk. Separation comes from a 1px
  `border` and the misregistered plate, not from a gray elevation step.
- `surface-foreground` is soy black. Body text, crop marks, rules, and the
  registration cross all use it.
- `primary` is the blue drum, the key action ink. `primary-foreground` is paper,
  not pure white — white looks like a screen.
- `accent` is the pink drum. It is the ghost plate (every `shadow-*`), the stamp
  ink, and the "on press" flourish. `accent-foreground` is paper, for type that
  sits on a pink fill.
- `ink-yellow` is the third drum, a fill only. Pair it with
  `ink-yellow-foreground` (soy black). Yellow never carries small type, and it
  is not a warning color.
- `danger` is a separate red drum for errors. It is not a brighter pink. Type on
  it uses `primary-foreground`.
- `muted` is a warm brown-gray for captions, job metadata, and secondary lines.
  Cool gray reads as a scanner, not a shop.
- `border` is soy black at full strength, drawn at 1px. A 4px frame belongs to
  a different system.
- One screen spends at most three inks plus paper and soy black. A fourth ink
  means a drum that is not loaded.
- Overlap is two plates multiplied, not a fourth color token. Do not invent a
  purple fill to fake the cross.

## Typography
System stacks only. No webfonts.
- Display and buttons: a heavy grotesque (`Arial Black`, Impact, then a bold
  system sans). `uppercase`, weight 800, tight negative tracking, line-height
  near 0.85. This is the poster voice, used for the job title and short
  actions — not for sentences.
- Body: a plain grotesque at regular weight, 16px, line-height 1.5. Measure
  stays near 65 characters. This is a job ticket, not a magazine column, so
  there is no serif prose face.
- Registration voice: a monospace, 11–12px, uppercase, tracked out. Job
  numbers, plate names, captions, and crop-mark labels use it. It is metadata,
  never a headline.
- Scale: display 64/76, H1 36/44, H2 24/28, H3 18/20, body 16, small 14,
  registration 12.
- The display color is `primary`, with a `text-shadow` in `accent` at
  `misregister-x` / `misregister-y` and zero blur. That shadow is the pink
  plate. Body text does not get it.

## Spacing & layout
- The sheet sits inset from the desk. Page padding 20 → 32. Sheet padding
  28 → 36, with extra room at the corners so crop marks (about 14px arms) do
  not cut the type.
- Section rhythm 64 → 80. Card padding 20 → 24.
- Gaps: 12, 16, 24, 32. The misregistered plate hangs to the right and below,
  so a gap under 12 lets the ghost collide with the next piece.
- The cover is a job desk: masthead, the edition on the bed, the queue. It is
  not a centered slogan with a single button.
- Asymmetry is mild. The poster block outweighs the copy, and the queue is a
  full-width ticket list under them. Broken grids and overlapping windows are a
  different style.
- Touch targets are 44px, 48px on a phone. Drums and dots are indicators, not
  targets, unless they sit inside a row that is itself 44px tall.

## Components
- **Crop marks:** 1px `border` arms at the four corners of a sheet. They mark a
  printable page. They are not decoration scattered through body copy.
- **Registration mark:** a soy circle with a cross through it, used once beside
  the wordmark. It is `radius-full` because it is a printer's mark, not a
  button.
- **Plates:** flat ink rectangles or circles. Halftone (`halftone` at
  `halftone-size`) sits inside the ink. Overlapping plates use multiply so the
  cross darkens. Plates do not carry body text; type sits above them.
- **Shadows:** `shadow-sm` on chips and fields, `shadow-md` on buttons,
  `shadow-lg` on the sheet and the poster. All zero blur, all the pink drum.
  `shadow-press` is the aligned plate (offset 0) for the active state.
- **Buttons:** square to `radius-md`, 1px soy border, heavy uppercase label,
  `shadow-md`. The primary action is a `primary` fill with
  `primary-foreground`. A quiet action is `surface-raised` with soy text. Hover
  shifts the piece up-left by 1px and lengthens the ghost. Active translates by
  the misregister and swaps to `shadow-press`, so the two plates line up under
  the thumb. Disabled drops the ghost, switches the border to dashed, and uses
  `muted` type — it reads as an empty drum, not a faded button.
- **Focus:** `shadow-focus`, a soy ring outside a paper gap. Never remove it
  without a replacement that is equally hard-edged.
- **Inputs:** `surface-raised` field, 1px soy rule, `radius-md`, `shadow-sm`.
  Focus fills the field with `ink-yellow` and `ink-yellow-foreground`. The
  yellow plate is how the shop says "this is the slot in use."
- **Chips:** status is a word plus an ink, not a dot alone. "On press" is
  `primary`, "drying" is `ink-yellow` with `ink-yellow-foreground`, "queued" is
  paper with a soy rule, "jam" is `danger` with `primary-foreground`.
- **Stamp:** a small mono label, `accent` border and text, rotated a few
  degrees, `shadow-sm`. One stamp per sheet. It is an edition mark, not a
  badge system.
- **Queue rows:** a ticket list. Index in mono, title in the grotesque, drums
  as tiny plates, status chip at the end. Rows are separated by 1px rules, not
  by cards floating in space.
- **Empty:** a dashed soy outline and a mono line ("No sheet on the bed"). No
  illustration, no gentle empty-state smile.
- **Error:** `danger` ink plus a mono reason ("Drum jam — pink"). Color is
  never the only signal.

## Motion
- Mechanical and short: `duration-shift` (120ms) on `ease-press`. The only
  travel is the plate sliding into or out of register.
- Hover lengthens the ghost. Active snaps it to zero. Nothing bounces, nothing
  fades up from transparent, nothing parallaxes.
- Halftone does not animate. A moving dot screen looks like a moiré error.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, drop the translation and keep the shadow
  change, so the press state is still visible.

## Accessibility
- Soy on `surface` and on `surface-raised` is the reading pair, well above
  7:1. `muted` on both clears 4.5:1 for captions and metadata only.
- `primary-foreground` on `primary`, on `accent`, and on `danger` each clears
  4.5:1. `accent` on `surface` and on `surface-raised` clears 4.5:1 for text,
  so pink labels are legal — pink as a large display fill still prefers paper
  type on top.
- `ink-yellow` fails for small type. Type on yellow is always
  `ink-yellow-foreground`.
- Halftone and paper tooth stay behind or inside large ink fields. They do not
  tile across paragraphs.
- State is never the offset alone. Pair the ghost with a fill, a label, or a
  border change. The focus ring is the keyboard affordance.

## Don't
- No blurred shadows, and no soft ambient lift.
- No gradients, mesh, or glass. A second plate is a flat ink shape offset from
  the first, not a fade between them.
- No radius above `radius-xl` (4px) except `radius-full` for drums and the
  registration mark. No pills, no 16px cards, no squishy corners.
- No 4px black poster frames, no hard black sticker shadow, no lime field, no
  polka-dot paper. Those are other systems.
- No beveled metal, no title-bar chrome, no pixel fonts.
- No inset white highlight and no clay sheen.
- No cool gray palette, no pure white sheet, no near-black "premium" page.
- No serif article column, no drop cap, no magazine pull-quote.
- No centered product-marketing hero as the cover. The cover is the desk.
- No extra drums. Three inks plus soy black plus paper.
- No halftone over type smaller than 16px.
- No opacity-only disabled state, and no pink used as the error color.
- No webfonts and no photographic paper texture. Tooth and halftone are drawn
  with the tokens above.
